1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: The Prophet — a person to whom Allah sends revelation and a divinely guided message for humankind. The word denotes one who conveys tidings from Allah, or (on another derivation) one of high and exalted rank.
2.grammar: A definite singular noun marked by the prefixed 'al-' ('the'). The doubling (shadda) on the nūn is not part of the base word: it results from the 'l' of 'al-' assimilating into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), so 'al-nabiyy' is pronounced 'an-nabiyy'. The base noun is نَبِيّ (nabiyy). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or the one being described.
2.root: Two derivations are held by grammarians: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, weighty information (one who brings tidings); or ن-ب-و (n-b-w) — to be high or elevated (one of exalted rank), favoured by those who note the doubled yāʾ pointing to an original wāw.

3.meaning: Guard yourself / be mindful and in awe of Allah; a command to adopt taqwā — a protective, reverent God-consciousness that shields one from wrongdoing and its consequences by keeping Allah ever in mind.

parts.en: guard yourself / be conscious of Allah!

3.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one masculine person: 'guard yourself (against), be in reverent awe (of).' It is a Form VIII pattern from the root for 'shielding/protecting.' The bare final -i (with no long vowel) is the clipped form the weak final root letter takes in the imperative, signalling the order is directed at a single 'you.'
3.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect; the source of taqwā (protective God-consciousness)

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

5.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
7.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
7.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

8.meaning: And the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief; people of a divided inner state who say one thing and hide another.
8.grammar: An active participle from Form III in the sound masculine plural. The prefix wa- means 'and'; al- is the definite article 'the'. The ending -īna is the sound masculine plural in its accusative or genitive form (the -ī vowel rather than -ū): it marks a group of males and signals that the word is a direct object, or is governed by a preposition or a preceding noun.
8.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — tunnel, hole; (Form III) to be two-faced, dissemble

9.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
9.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

11.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

11.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

12.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
12.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

13.meaning: All-Wise; one possessing perfect wisdom, who places everything in its right place and decides with flawless judgement. As an intensive form it conveys wisdom that is complete and sound.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-wise') on the faʿīl pattern, stressing the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: 'It is revealed / inspired' — for a message to be conveyed by Allah to a prophet, whether by inspiration, sign, or revealed word. This is the passive sense: the revelation is sent to the recipient.

parts.en: he/it (third-person masculine present prefix, passive vowel)
is revealed / inspired (passive stem ending in a long final vowel)

3.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice: the 'yu-' prefix with the internal vowel pattern means 'it is (being) revealed' — the action is done TO the subject. The verb ends in a fixed long '-ā' vowel because its final root letter is weak; this form is the same in the passive present regardless of case.
3.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — revelation, inspiration, conveying a message

4.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
4.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: The Lord belonging to a single male 'you' — Rabb is the Master, Owner, and Sustainer who creates, nurtures, and brings to maturity; here 'your Lord'.
6.grammar: The noun rabb (Lord, Sustainer) with the attached pronoun -ka, 'your' for one male. The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, the case that typically links a word to a following possessor or follows a preposition (here showing the possession 'of you'). The doubled b (shadda) belongs to the root.

7.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
7.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

9.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
10.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

11.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
11.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

12.meaning: Deeply aware, well-acquainted, fully informed — one whose knowledge penetrates the inner realities and hidden details of things. As a divine attribute of Allah, the All-Aware.
12.grammar: An adjective on the pattern faʿīl meaning 'thoroughly acquainted with inner realities.' The -an ending is the indefinite accusative: here it functions as a predicate complement ('… is all-aware') in clauses that take an accusative predicate, and the doubled nasal -n (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite.
12.root: خ-ب-ر (kh-b-r) — to know thoroughly, be acquainted with the inner truth of things; inner knowledge

2.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
2.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
2.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
4.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
4.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

5.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
5.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

6.meaning: A trustee, guardian, or disposer of affairs — one to whom matters are committed and who is relied upon to manage and protect them.
6.grammar: A noun on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('one who is relied upon'). The '-an' ending (with tanwīn) marks the indefinite accusative case: it commonly signals the object of a verb, or the role/capacity in which something serves ('as a …').
6.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — entrusting, reliance, appointing someone to manage one's affairs

1.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
1.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

2.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
9.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

10.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'

14.meaning: A small phrase meaning 'from them' or 'of them,' referring to a group of females. It combines the preposition min (from, of, some of) with an attached 'them' (feminine).
14.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. Min means 'from,' 'out of,' or 'some of.' The pronoun -hunna means 'them' for a group of females; after the n of min it keeps its base vowel -u (hunna). The combination commonly expresses source, origin, or a part taken from a whole.

15.meaning: Your mothers — the plural of 'mother,' addressed to a group, denoting the women who gave you birth.
15.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun with the attached pronoun -kum ('your,' addressed to several people). The -i before the pronoun marks the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive '… OF …' construction.

16.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
16.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

17.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'

19.meaning: 'Your sons / your children' — the male offspring (or offspring generally) belonging to the addressed group.
19.grammar: A masculine plural noun ('sons') with the attached possessive -kum ('your,' to a group). The -a ending is the accusative, which typically marks the object of a verb. The case vowel sits before the pronoun suffix.

20.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
20.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

23.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
23.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
23.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

24.meaning: 'He says' or 'he is saying' — the act of speaking or uttering words. The imperfect tense conveys an ongoing, habitual, or present/future action.
24.grammar: Imperfect (present/future) verb, third person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he', the stem qūl carries the meaning 'say', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement (as opposed to a subjunctive -a or jussive sukūn used after certain particles).

25.meaning: The truth — that which is real, right, and established; reality, the just due, the genuine as opposed to the false.
25.grammar: A definite noun with 'the'. The -a ending is the accusative, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the truth').
25.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is established and real

26.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
26.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

27.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
27.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
27.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

28.meaning: 'The way, the path, the road' — used both for a physical route and, very commonly, for the figurative 'path' of right conduct, religion, or a course of action.
28.grammar: A definite noun: the al- prefix means 'the'. The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or signals an adverbial sense.

2.meaning: For/to their fathers (or forefathers) — belonging to or directed toward the ancestors. Combines 'for/to', the plural 'fathers', and 'their'.
2.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (for/to) attached to a broken (irregular) plural noun, with the pronoun 'their' suffixed. The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, required after a preposition; the -him form of 'their' is the variant used after an i-sound. Sense: 'for their fathers'.

3.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
3.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

4.meaning: More/most just, equitable, or fair — a comparative-superlative adjective (elative) built from the sense of justice and fair dealing. It expresses a higher degree of fairness ('more just', or 'most just').
4.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) on the afʿal pattern, where the a- prefix conveys 'more' or 'most'. The -u ending is nominative, marking it as a subject or predicate (the thing being described) rather than an object. This form does not take tanwīn.

5.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
5.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
7.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

8.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
8.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

9.meaning: You (plural) know, understand, or have knowledge of something — grasping a fact with certainty.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ū ending makes it masculine plural ('you all'). The short, vowelless -ū (not -ūna) is the jussive/subjunctive shape, used after particles of command, negation, or purpose ('until you know' / 'so that you know').

11.meaning: 'Then they are your brothers' — kinsfolk or brethren who belong to your own group, here a plural 'brothers' joined to 'your'.
11.grammar: A plural noun with the prefix fa- ('then, so', often introducing a result) and the attached pronoun -kum ('your', addressing a group), which makes it definite by possession. The -u before the pronoun reflects the nominative case, used here for a predicate ('they are your brothers').

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: A term for 'the religion, the faith, the way of life and obedience owed to Allah'. It covers belief, worship, law, and the system of accountability and recompense — broader than the English word 'religion'.
13.grammar: A definite noun ('the religion'); the al- prefix means 'the'. The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of …').
13.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, judgment, requital, obedience, debt

15.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not.' It denies that something is currently the case, functioning to negate a statement in the present, and it inflects for person like a verb.
15.grammar: A hollow negating verb fixed in form for the third-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'); the -a ending belongs to its frozen past-tense shape. Though past in form, it negates in the present. It introduces a subject and a predicate, denying the link between them. The prefix wa means 'and'.

16.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
16.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

17.meaning: Blame, fault, or sin incurred by an action; a moral lapse for which one is held accountable. In Qur'anic usage it most often appears in the phrase 'there is no junāḥ', i.e. no blame or wrongdoing attaches to doing something.
17.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -un (nominative case with nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a blame / any sin') and signals that it functions as a subject or the noun of existence ('there is a …'). The nunation (the -n sound) is the mark of indefiniteness.
17.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline or lean away (hence to deviate toward wrongdoing; the root also yields 'wing' and 'side')

18.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
18.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

20.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
20.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

21.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
21.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

22.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
22.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

24.meaning: 'Your hearts.' The plural of 'heart' — the inner seat of feeling, thought, intention, and faith — joined to 'your' (referring to a group).
24.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') with an attached possessive 'your'. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject — the doer or the thing being described. The -kum ('your') refers to a group including males.
24.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about

25.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
25.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

26.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
26.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

27.meaning: A word meaning 'much-forgiving' or 'ever-forgiving' — an intensive form describing one whose forgiveness is abundant and constant. It is one of the qualities of Allah.
27.grammar: An intensive adjective on the pattern faʿūl, conveying that the quality is great in degree and repeated. The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite 'n' sound), written with a supporting alif; it is the form an indefinite word takes when it is, for example, a predicate of certain verbs/particles or otherwise placed in the object position.

28.meaning: 'Most Merciful / deeply compassionate' — an intensive form of raḥima, denoting one full of mercy and tender compassion; a frequent description of Allah.
28.grammar: An intensive adjective on the fa'īl pattern, expressing a deep, abiding quality — abounding in mercy. The -an ending is the accusative case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n,' often marking it as a predicate or as describing someone as 'most merciful.'

2.meaning: More entitled, more deserving, closer in claim or priority. A comparative meaning 'worthier (of)' or 'having a stronger right (to)'.
2.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) adjective on the pattern afʿalu, expressing 'more X' or 'most X'. It is invariable in this spelling, ending in a long final ā, and is typically followed by 'than' or by the thing one has a claim to.

3.meaning: With/in the believers — 'the believers' being those who have faith, who trust and affirm and are inwardly secure in belief. The word combines a preposition meaning 'with/by/in/toward' and the definite plural 'the believers'.
3.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with/by/toward') attached to the definite noun 'the believers'. The noun is in the genitive case — its sound masculine plural ending is -īna here — because words after a preposition take the genitive. The plural -īn(a) refers to three or more males (or a mixed group).

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: Themselves / their own selves — the noun nafs ('self, soul, person, inner being') joined to a pronoun 'their'. Used reflexively it means 'their own selves' and conveys the inmost self, the seat of desires and the person as a whole.
5.grammar: The plural noun anfus ('selves') carries the genitive -i ending followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -him makes it 'their selves'.
5.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

8.meaning: And those possessing — 'and the owners/holders of …', a plural construct meaning 'people endowed with' or 'masters of' whatever follows. 'Ulū' has no singular of its own form and always leads into a following noun.
8.grammar: A masculine plural noun meaning 'possessors/owners of', preceded by 'wa' ('and'). It exists only in a possessive ('… of …') construction and must be followed by another noun naming what is possessed. The '-ū' ending is the masculine plural form used for a subject; in this bound state it has dropped its final 'n', linking it to the following noun.
8.root: — (a plural noun used only in construct; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: The wombs; by extension, ties of kinship and blood relationship. The plural of the noun for the womb, often evoking the bonds among relatives.
9.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun on the afʿāl pattern, made definite by the article al-. The final -i ending is genitive, the case typically used after a preposition, after an oath, or to link the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

10.meaning: 'Some of them' / 'a part of them' — a noun meaning 'a portion, part, or some' joined to an attached pronoun 'them'. Often paired with itself to express 'one another / each other'.
10.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the nominative case (the -u ending), which typically marks it as the subject or doer. The suffix -hum is a genitive (possessive) pronoun meaning 'their' (masculine plural); attached to a noun this way it sits in the possessor slot, giving 'some of them'.
10.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

11.meaning: More entitled, more deserving, closer in claim or priority. A comparative meaning 'worthier (of)' or 'having a stronger right (to)'.
11.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) adjective on the pattern afʿalu, expressing 'more X' or 'most X'. It is invariable in this spelling, ending in a long final ā, and is typically followed by 'than' or by the thing one has a claim to.

12.meaning: 'In part / in some' — referring to a portion or some of a whole, here left indefinite. The bi- prefix gives the sense of disbelieving 'in' something.
12.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with') plus the noun baʿḍ ('a part, some'). The final -in (tanwīn kasr) is the genitive case with indefiniteness, required after bi- and marking the noun as 'some (unspecified) part.'
12.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: A scripture or book; in particular a written revelation. The word denotes something written down and consigned to record — a 'Book' in the sense of a divinely sent, recorded scripture, also carrying the broader sense of a binding decree or anything set down in writing.
14.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -i ending is genitive (the 'of' case): it typically marks the word as linked to a following noun ('… OF …'), or as governed by a preceding preposition or oath particle.

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
16.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

17.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
17.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

18.meaning: And the emigrants — those who left their homes and migrated for the sake of faith, abandoning one place for another. The leading 'and' joins it to a preceding item; the rest is a plural active participle naming such migrants as a class.
18.grammar: 'And' (wa) + al- ('the') + a Form III active participle ('one who migrates'); Form III often carries a sense of mutual or directed action. The -īna ending is a masculine sound plural in the object or prepositional (accusative/genitive) case — the form used when such a word is an object or follows a preposition, as opposed to subject-case -ūna.

19.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
19.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

20.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
20.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

21.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) do/make/act' — referring to an action carried out by a group being addressed. Built on the very common root for doing or performing a deed, it is the standard word for engaging in or carrying out an act.
21.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural. The ta- prefix signals a 'you' subject; the -ū ending marks a plural ('you all'). The bare -ū without a final nūn (rather than -ūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form used after particles of negation, purpose, or condition.

22.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
22.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

24.meaning: Kind / fitting / recognized as good — that which is commonly acknowledged as right and decent; honorable speech or conduct that accords with reason and custom. A rich term denoting what is universally seen as fair and proper.

parts.en: what is good / recognized as right

24.grammar: A passive participle (literally 'that which is known/recognized') used as a noun and adjective for goodness. The -an ending (accusative with nunation) commonly marks it as a direct object or a description ('in a fitting way'). The doubled-n sound signals indefiniteness ('a …').
24.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — knowing, recognizing; hence what is recognized and acknowledged as good

25.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

25.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

26.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
26.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

27.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
27.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

28.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
28.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

29.meaning: Written down, inscribed, recorded line by line — a passive participle describing something set down in writing.
29.grammar: A passive participle (describing what receives the action — that which 'is written') on the pattern maf'ūl. The ending -an is accusative and indefinite; this 'tanwīn' commonly marks an indefinite predicate or object.
29.root: س-ط-ر (s-ṭ-r) — to write in lines, inscribe, set down

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: "We took / seized / received" — to take, take hold of, seize, or accept; with a pact it means to bind a party to a covenant. The form carries a 'we' subject.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with the attached subject suffix '-nā' meaning 'we': it marks a completed action done by a group (or the royal/majestic 'We'). The '-nā' ending is what turns the bare verb into 'we did it'.

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: 'The prophets' — those whom Allah selects to receive revelation and convey His message. The plural of nabī, a prophet who brings news from Allah.
4.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the genitive-or-accusative case — the form used when the noun is a direct object or governed by a preposition, as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject.
4.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; hence a prophet who brings news from Allah

5.meaning: 'Their solemn pledge / covenant.' The noun denotes a firmly bound, ratified agreement — a compact made binding and tightly tied, from a root meaning to make fast and secure.
5.grammar: A noun (an instrument-type form meaning 'that by which something is bound fast') with the attached possessive -hum ('their'). The -a vowel on the noun is the accusative ending, which typically marks it as the object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
5.root: و-ث-ق (w-th-q) — to bind firmly, make fast, trust

7.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
7.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

10.meaning: 'And Moses (Mūsā)' — the proper name of the prophet, prefixed with 'and'.
10.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin prefixed with 'wa' ('and'). It ends in a fixed long '-ā' (written as alif maqṣūra) and so shows no visible change for case.

11.meaning: And ʿĪsā (Jesus) — the proper name of the Prophet Jesus, son of Mary; with the prefixed 'and'.
11.grammar: A proper name (the Prophet Jesus) preceded by the conjunction wa- ('and'). As a foreign/indeclinable name ending in a long -ā, it does not change its ending for case — it keeps the same form whether it functions as subject, object, or possessor.

12.meaning: 'Son (of)' — a male child or descendant; commonly used to link a person to their father or lineage.
12.grammar: A singular masculine noun meaning 'son.' The '-i' ending is genitive — the state a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a following noun ('son OF …'). This word characteristically stands between two names, joining a person to his father in a chain of descent.
12.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — son, offspring; to build

13.meaning: Maryam (Mary), a proper name. It is the name of the revered woman honored in Islam as the mother of the Prophet ʿĪsā (Jesus).
13.grammar: A proper noun (a personal name). Being a foreign/non-Arabic name and feminine, it is 'diptote': it does not take tanwīn (the -un/-an/-in nunation) and shows only a single -a vowel for both the accusative and genitive. The -a ending marks it as a direct object (the one being acted upon) or as governed by a preposition.

14.meaning: 'And We took / received / seized.' A first-person plural past-tense verb from the root meaning 'to take.' It conveys a completed act of taking hold of something — and idiomatically, of taking a pledge or covenant FROM someone, i.e. binding them to it.
14.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb expressing a completed action. The attached -nā ending is the first-person plural subject 'we,' so the whole word means 'we took.' The prefixed wa- simply joins this statement to what precedes it ('and').
14.root: ا-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, take hold of

15.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
15.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

17.meaning: Thick, dense, heavy, and severe — describing something coarse and weighty rather than light or flimsy. Applied to a pledge it means a grave and solemn one; applied generally it suggests harshness or toughness.
17.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong or established quality. The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and accusative — the case that typically matches a noun it describes when that noun stands as an object.

2.meaning: The truthful ones — those who are sincere and speak the truth, whose words and deeds match reality. A plural describing people characterized by truthfulness and sincerity, prefixed with 'the.'
2.grammar: A masculine plural active participle ('the ones who are truthful') with the definite article 'the.' The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive (oblique) form: it marks the word either as an object of a verb or as following a preposition or possessive, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
2.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, telling the truth

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

3.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

5.meaning: 'And He prepared / made ready' — a perfect verb meaning to ready, arrange, or set in store something in advance; here joined by 'and'.
5.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus a perfect verb (form IV), 3rd-person masculine singular. It states a completed act, 'he prepared'; the doubled final consonant reflects this form's pattern.

6.meaning: A three-part word: 'for' + 'the' + 'those who cover up the truth / reject faith.' The base noun denotes the kāfir — one who disbelieves, denies, and ungratefully conceals the truth and Allah's favor. With 'for,' it marks them as the ones for whom something is intended.
6.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a definite plural noun, masculine. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, here required because it follows the preposition 'li-'. The whole denotes 'for the disbelievers.'
6.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

7.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
7.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

8.meaning: An adjective meaning 'painful / agonizing'. It describes something that causes intense pain or suffering, whether physical or anguishing.
8.grammar: An adjective in the intensive faʿīl pattern ('intensely ___'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a painful [one]'), the case typically taken by a noun/adjective serving as an object or agreeing with one.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'Remember! / call to mind, mention' — a command to bring something to mind, keep it in memory, or speak of it.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you.' The '-ū' ending directs the order to a group ('you all remember!'); the initial connecting 'a-' is a helping vowel that lets the word begin.

5.meaning: Favour, blessing, or grace; a bestowed benefit or state of ease and well-being granted as a gift, especially divine favour.
5.grammar: A noun meaning favour or blessing. The -a ending is accusative: it typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
7.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
8.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

9.meaning: 'She/it has come to you (plural)' — a completed act of coming/arriving, with a feminine subject reaching a plural 'you.'
9.grammar: Past-tense verb 'to come.' The '-at' suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it came.' The attached '-kum' is the object 'you all' (masculine plural). Together: 'she/it has come to you.'

11.meaning: So We sent / dispatched — to send forth a messenger, a message, or (as here) something loosed upon people. The form has the subject 'we'.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the form IV pattern (arsala, 'to send'), with the attached subject pronoun -nā ('we'). The fa- prefix marks consequence or sequence ('so, then'). The -nā ending shows that 'we' performed the completed action.

12.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
12.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
12.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

15.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
15.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

16.meaning: You see it / you saw it — to perceive with the eyes, to behold. Ra'ā is the basic verb of visual sight (and, more broadly, of perceiving or considering).
16.grammar: A present-tense verb in the second person masculine plural with an attached object pronoun -hā ('it', feminine/non-human). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and (in the jussive mood, typically after a negation meaning 'did not') the plural lost its final -na, leaving the bare stem before the pronoun — giving the sense 'you (all) did not see it'.

17.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
17.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

19.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
19.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

20.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
20.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

21.meaning: All-Seeing — one who sees fully and perfectly. An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) expressing sight as a permanent, comprehensive attribute that misses nothing.
21.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or a predicate after certain particles — and the -n shows it is indefinite ('a seer / seeing').

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: They came to you / they reached you — a completed act of a group arriving at or approaching addressees.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the attached -kum is the plural object ('you all'), so together the verb means 'they came to you'. The perfect tense presents the action as already completed.

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

4.meaning: Above you (plural), over you — the region overhead or a higher position relative to a group. 'Your' refers to the group.
4.grammar: A location word ('above') with an attached possessive. The -i ending is the genitive, expected here because such location words behave like the first term of an 'of' phrase; the attached -kum means 'you all / your'.
4.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above, to surpass

5.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
5.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

6.meaning: Lower, lowest, further down. A comparative/superlative adjective denoting the lower position or the bottommost of things.
6.grammar: An adjective of the 'afʿal' (comparative/superlative) pattern meaning 'lower/lowest'. The -a ending here marks the accusative, which commonly serves an adverbial sense of place ('further down / in a lower position') or marks the word as an object/complement.
6.root: س-ف-ل (s-f-l) — lowness, being beneath, the bottom

7.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
7.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
7.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

8.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
8.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

10.meaning: The eyes; the seeing faculties or sights — the organs of vision (a plural of 'baṣar,' eyesight).
10.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun meaning 'eyes / faculties of sight,' made definite by al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.
10.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — to see, perceive, have sight/insight

12.meaning: The hearts — the inner seats of feeling, understanding, intention, and faith. In Arabic the heart (qalb) is the core of the person where conviction and emotion reside, not merely the organ.
12.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, 'hearts', made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject or doer of a sentence — the one performing or undergoing the action.
12.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart, turning, the inmost core

14.meaning: And you suppose, think, reckon, or presume; to hold an opinion or conjecture. The root spans from uncertain guessing to firm assumption, depending on context.
14.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and.' The verb is present tense; the prefix ta- marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks a male plural in an ongoing or future action: 'and you suppose / will think.'

15.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
15.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
15.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

1.meaning: An adverb meaning 'there' or 'at that point' — pointing to a distant place, and by extension to a particular moment or set of circumstances ('right then and there').
1.grammar: A demonstrative adverb of place built from hunā ('there') plus the suffix -lika that signals farness, giving 'over there / yonder'. It is a fixed (indeclinable) word with no changing case ending, and can point to a time or situation as well as a place.

3.meaning: The believers — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm the truth and give it their security and assent.
3.grammar: A definite noun, the active participle of form IV ('mu'min,' 'one who believes/grants security'). The plural ending '-ūna' marks a masculine human plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or doer ('the believers' as those performing the action).

4.meaning: To be shaken, convulsed, or violently disturbed — to be rocked back and forth, as by upheaval, fear, or trial.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (the subjects had the action done to them — they 'were shaken' rather than 'shook'). The prefix wa- means 'and'. The ending -ū marks a masculine plural doer/undergoer, 'they'.
4.root: ز-ل-ز-ل (z-l-z-l) — to shake violently, to convulse; quaking

6.meaning: 'Severe / intense / harsh.' An adjective describing something strong, forceful, and hard to bear.
6.grammar: An adjective in an intensive pattern ('very strong/severe'). The -an ending marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the form used when it describes a noun that is itself indefinite and accusative.
6.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, severe

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: 'He says' or 'he is saying' — the act of speaking or uttering words. The imperfect tense conveys an ongoing, habitual, or present/future action.
2.grammar: Imperfect (present/future) verb, third person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he', the stem qūl carries the meaning 'say', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement (as opposed to a subjunctive -a or jussive sukūn used after certain particles).

3.meaning: 'The hypocrites' — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief or treachery; the term pictures someone who has a hidden 'tunnel' or back-exit out of their professed commitment.
3.grammar: A definite plural noun (an active participle, 'the ones who dissemble'). The al- prefix means 'the'. The -ūna ending marks a masculine sound plural in the nominative case, the form typically used when the noun is the doer/subject.
3.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to tunnel through, dissemble; hypocrisy

4.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
4.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the plural of qalb ('heart'), joined to the pronoun 'their'. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' (qalb) is the seat of understanding, intention, faith, and feeling, not merely the physical organ.
6.grammar: Qulūb is the broken (irregular) plural of qalb, 'hearts'. The -i ending is genitive: here it appears because the noun follows a preposition and because it is possessed by an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'their' (a masculine plural group), and its -i- vowel matches the preceding genitive ending. So the whole means 'hearts belonging to them'.
6.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about, change

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'a disease,' 'sickness,' or 'ailment' — a disorder that afflicts the body, and figuratively a corruption or malady of the heart (such as doubt, hypocrisy, or ill intent).
7.grammar: A common noun, masculine singular. The final '-un' (nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a disease') and in the nominative case, which typically identifies it as a subject or as the thing stated to exist. (When the word follows another ending in a consonant, that consonant may assimilate onto its first letter in recitation, but this gemination is external and not part of the word itself.)
7.root: م-ر-ض (m-r-ḍ) — to be sick, diseased, ailing

8.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
8.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

9.meaning: He promised us / pledged to us — to make a binding promise or commitment, expressed as a completed past act by a single male, with 'us' as the recipients of the promise.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb. The bare stem with the '-a' vowel marks the subject as a single male ('he'), and the attached '-nā' is the object 'us'. The past tense frames the promise as already given.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
10.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

11.meaning: "And His Messenger," the one sent with a message; "rasūl" denotes an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver something, here belonging to "Him."
11.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The base "rasūl" is a noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning "one who is sent." The suffix "-hu" is the attached possessive pronoun "his," placing the noun in a possessive "messenger of Him" relationship; the pronoun occupies the genitive slot.
11.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message or the one sent with it

12.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
12.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

13.meaning: 'delusion / deception / vain beguilement' — the deceiving of someone with empty, alluring appearances so that they are lulled into false confidence.
13.grammar: A noun with the -an ending (indefinite accusative, 'tanwīn'), which typically marks an indefinite 'a …' functioning as an object or, often, as a description of manner ('… as a delusion / deceptively'). It names the act/quality of beguiling deception.
13.root: غ-ر-ر (gh-r-r) — to deceive, delude, beguile; vanity

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: She said — a completed act of speaking or saying, attributed to a single female.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -at ending that marks a single female doer ('she said'). The plain past form presents the action as a completed whole.

3.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a distinct band or section of people, often a smaller portion of a larger body.
3.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a group', not 'the group') and in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence.
3.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, circle; a portion that moves about

4.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
4.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

5.meaning: 'O people of… / O folk of…' — a vocative call ('O!') addressed to the 'people' or 'folk' belonging to something (such as the people of a household, place, or scripture).
5.grammar: The vocative particle ya ('O') used to address or call out, plus the noun 'people/folk'. The -a ending is accusative, which is the case a called-upon noun takes when it is attached to a following word ('O people OF …'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with something.
5.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, those belonging to

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
9.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

12.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a portion or section of people set apart from a larger body.
12.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The '-un' (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ('a group') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence.
12.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide; a division

14.meaning: 'The prophet' — a person to whom Allah sends revelation and inspired tidings to convey to people.
14.grammar: A noun made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into that state. It denotes a recipient and bearer of prophetic revelation.
14.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — momentous news, tidings (hence 'prophet,' bearer of revealed news)

15.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
15.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

16.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
