14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

16.meaning: Mighty, all-powerful, invincible — one who is dominant and cannot be overcome; also carrying the sense of precious and held in high honor. Of a person it means strong and unassailable.
16.grammar: An intensive adjective (of the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, settled quality). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, which typically signals a direct object or a descriptive complement governed into the accusative.
16.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, dominance; also honor and preciousness

1.meaning: 'And He sent down / caused to descend'. It denotes bringing something down from a higher place to a lower one — characteristically the sending down of revelation. Past tense, third person masculine singular.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is the connector 'and'. 'anzala' is a past-tense verb of the causative pattern (form IV) meaning 'to make descend / send down', with the third-person masculine singular subject ('he') built in; the final '-a' is the standard past-tense ending.
1.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, send down

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: People of / folk of / those belonging to — the family, followers, or possessors of something (as in 'people of the Book'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with a thing.
5.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/folk of'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('people OF …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.
5.root: ء-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, people belonging to

6.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
6.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: A noun meaning 'hearts' — the plural of the heart, understood as the inner seat of feeling, understanding, intention, and faith, not merely the physical organ.
11.grammar: A plural noun. The -i vowel on the stem is the genitive ending, which links the noun to what follows or follows a preposition ('… of …'); the attached -him(u) means 'their', so together it reads 'their hearts'. The final short -u is a connecting vowel that smooths pronunciation before the next word.

12.meaning: Terror, dread, intense fear — overwhelming fright that grips and unsettles a person. 'Ruʿb' is a fear that fills and shakes the heart.
12.grammar: A noun ('terror') with the -a ending, marking the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb ('… the terror'). With 'al-' ('the') it is definite. The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'r' (pronounced ar-ruʿba).
12.root: ر-ع-ب (r-ʿ-b) — to fill with dread, to terrify

13.meaning: A group, faction, party, or portion of people — a section split off from a larger body.
13.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an (tanwīn fatḥ) ending marks the accusative case with indefiniteness, typically signalling the direct object of a verb ('a group'), or an adverbial sense.

14.meaning: You kill, you slay — to put to death, to take life. The verb denotes the act of killing.
14.grammar: Present/future-tense verb addressed to a group ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks second person 'you'; the -ūna ending marks masculine-plural subjects together with the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact, 'you do/will kill'), unlike a command or a subjunctive/jussive form which would drop the final -na.
14.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay, put to death

16.meaning: A group, faction, party, or portion of people — a section split off from a larger body.
16.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an (tanwīn fatḥ) ending marks the accusative case with indefiniteness, typically signalling the direct object of a verb ('a group'), or an adverbial sense.

4.meaning: And their wealth / their possessions — material property and riches belonging to them (a group), joined with 'and' and the pronoun 'their'.
4.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') joined to the plural noun 'amwāl' ('wealth/properties') with the attached possessive '-hum' ('their'). The '-a' before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case typically used when the noun is the direct object of a verb. 'amwāl' is itself a broken plural of 'māl' (property).

6.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
6.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

8.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
9.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

11.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
11.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

12.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
12.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
12.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: The Prophet — a person to whom Allah sends revelation and a divinely guided message for humankind. The word denotes one who conveys tidings from Allah, or (on another derivation) one of high and exalted rank.
2.grammar: A definite singular noun marked by the prefixed 'al-' ('the'). The doubling (shadda) on the nūn is not part of the base word: it results from the 'l' of 'al-' assimilating into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), so 'al-nabiyy' is pronounced 'an-nabiyy'. The base noun is نَبِيّ (nabiyy). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or the one being described.
2.root: Two derivations are held by grammarians: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, weighty information (one who brings tidings); or ن-ب-و (n-b-w) — to be high or elevated (one of exalted rank), favoured by those who note the doubled yāʾ pointing to an original wāw.

3.meaning: An imperative command meaning 'Say!' or 'Speak!' — a direct order to one person to utter or declare something.
3.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male. The bare, vowelless ending (the silent stop on the final 'l') marks it as a direct order: 'you, say!' It is built from the verb 'to say' with the weak middle letter dropped, leaving the short, clipped command form.
3.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

5.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
5.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

8.meaning: "the life" — the state of being alive; living existence, vitality.
8.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -a ending (on the feminine -t) is accusative, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb or the noun governed by certain particles.

9.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
9.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
9.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

10.meaning: And its adornment / its finery. 'zīna' is decoration, ornament, beauty, or the attractive splendour with which something is made appealing. The attached pronoun makes it 'its adornment'; the leading 'wa' means 'and'.
10.grammar: A feminine noun with 'wa' ('and') in front and the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her') at the end. The '-a' ending before the pronoun is accusative, the case marking a noun that is the object of a verb or otherwise governed in that role. The '-hā' shows possession by a feminine or grammatically feminine thing: 'its adornment'.

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

5.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
5.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hereafter / the next life / the world to come' — literally 'the last (abode)', the final, everlasting existence following this present life.
7.grammar: A definite noun (al- = 'the') bearing the -a ending, which marks the accusative (object) case — the form a noun takes when it is the object of a verb. It is feminine in form (the tā' marbūṭa ending).
7.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after; lastness, the end

8.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
8.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
9.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

10.meaning: He has prepared / made ready — to set something up in advance, to ready or get it in order beforehand.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he prepared'). It belongs to the 'form IV' pattern (the a- prefix gives the sense of actively making something ready). With no added subject suffix, the bare form means 'he' did the action, completed in the past. The doubled middle letter (shadda) is part of this root.
10.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — to count, prepare, make ready

13.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
13.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
13.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

14.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
14.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

2.meaning: The Prophet — a person who receives revelation from Allah and announces it, one given prophetic news and inspired tidings from the unseen.
2.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'the'. The final -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive chain, follows a preposition, or marks agreement with a preceding genitive word. The article's l assimilates into the following n (an-nabiy), since n is a 'sun letter'.
2.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; to inform, announce

3.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
3.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'he comes' or 'he brings about' — to arrive, approach, or come forward; can also mean to do or produce something.
4.grammar: A present/future verb. The ya- prefix marks the doer as 'he' (a single male). The shortened final -i (the weak final letter being dropped) reflects the jussive/apocopate form, which typically appears after conditional or negative particles and in commands.
4.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, approach; to bring or do

6.meaning: A noun preceded by 'with,' built on the word for a gross indecency — an outrageous, shameful, morally excessive act; sexual immorality or any flagrant transgression.
6.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The tāʾ marbūṭa (-at) marks it as a feminine singular noun denoting the act itself. The final -in (tanwīn kasra) is the indefinite genitive ending ('a …'), the case regularly required after a preposition.

7.meaning: An adjective meaning 'made clear, manifest, plainly evident' — describing something that has been openly shown or is unmistakable.
7.grammar: An active participle of the intensive form-II pattern (mubayyina), meaning 'one that makes clear / is manifest.' The mu- prefix forms the participle; the -at marks feminine agreement; the final -in (tanwīn kasra) is the indefinite genitive — the case used to agree with a preceding genitive noun or after a preposition.

9.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
9.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

10.meaning: "the punishment / torment" — a painful penalty or chastisement inflicted as retribution; suffering imposed as a consequence.
10.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks the subject of a verb or the doer/topic of a sentence.

11.meaning: Twofold, double, or two times over — twice the usual amount.
11.grammar: A dual noun (referring to exactly two). The '-ayni' ending marks the dual in the accusative/genitive — the special form Arabic uses for a pair, here meaning 'a double, twice as much'.
11.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — to double, multiply; a multiple, fold

12.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

13.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
13.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

14.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
14.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
14.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: 'Easy, effortless, slight, manageable.' It describes something simple to do or small in amount.
16.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('an easy …'), commonly marking an adjective agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or a verb's object/complement.
16.root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — to be easy, light, manageable

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

4.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
4.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
5.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
5.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

7.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
7.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
7.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

10.meaning: Two times, twice — exactly two occurrences of something. It is the dual ('exactly two') form of the noun meaning 'a time/instance'.
10.grammar: A dual noun, meaning 'exactly two' of the thing. The -ayni ending marks the dual in the accusative or genitive state; for an adverb of frequency this conveys 'two times / twice'. Arabic has a special dual distinct from the plural (three or more).
10.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — to pass by; a passing, hence an instance/time

11.meaning: And We have made ready — to prepare, arrange, and set something in store beforehand so it stands waiting.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb (form VIII) prefixed with 'wa' (and). The 't' in the stem is the form VIII infix, not a root letter. The suffix '-nā' is the subject ending meaning 'we (did it),' marking a completed action performed by a first-person plural — an act already accomplished.
11.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — counting, reckoning; readying and setting in store (form VIII اعتدّ, with the doubled dāl, from this root)

12.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
12.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

13.meaning: 'provision,' 'sustenance,' 'a means of livelihood' — that which is bestowed to sustain and benefit, such as food and resources. 'Rizq' is whatever Allah grants a creature to live on, material or otherwise.
13.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks the accusative case with indefiniteness — frequently the role of a stated purpose or explanatory complement ('as provision'), telling for what reason or in what capacity something is given.

14.meaning: Noble, generous, honourable — describing something or someone of high worth, dignity, and openhanded goodness. Used of provision, status, or character that is precious and held in honour.
14.grammar: An adjective in the indefinite accusative. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks the indefinite accusative case, which typically signals the object of a verb or a descriptive/adverbial role, in an unspecified, non-particular sense ('a noble/generous one').

2.meaning: The Prophet — a person who receives revelation from Allah and announces it, one given prophetic news and inspired tidings from the unseen.
2.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'the'. The final -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive chain, follows a preposition, or marks agreement with a preceding genitive word. The article's l assimilates into the following n (an-nabiy), since n is a 'sun letter'.
2.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; to inform, announce

5.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
5.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

6.meaning: 'The women' — the plural used for women/females collectively. (It serves as the plural of mar'a, 'woman.')
6.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or standing in a possessive ('of …') relationship. The l of al- assimilates into the following n in pronunciation (a 'sun letter').

7.meaning: If — a particle introducing a condition: it sets up 'if X (happens), then Y'.
7.grammar: A conditional particle ('if') that introduces a supposed case and typically puts the following verb into the jussive (conditional) form. Its base shape is 'in', whose final nūn carries a sukūn and is fully pronounced. When the next word begins with a sukūn-bearing cluster, the otherwise-quiescent nūn is given a kasra (-i) to avoid two consecutive sukūns meeting (the 'meeting of two quiescents'); this helping vowel eases pronunciation and carries no grammatical meaning of its own.

9.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
9.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

11.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with/by the saying' or 'with the word/statement'. It combines the preposition 'bi-' (with, by means of) with 'al-qawl', a verbal noun meaning an act of speech, an utterance, a statement, or a word that is spoken.
11.grammar: A preposition ('bi-', with/by) attached to a definite noun. The preposition forces the genitive case, which is why the noun ends in '-i' rather than '-u'. The '-i' ending here is the mark of a noun governed by a preposition, conveying the sense 'with the saying' or 'by means of the word'.
11.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

13.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
13.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
14.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

15.meaning: 'His heart' — the heart as the inner seat of thought, feeling, intention, and faith.
15.grammar: A noun ('heart') with the possessive pronoun -hi ('his') attached. The -i before the pronoun marks the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or as the second part of a possessive pair. (The pronoun is voweled -hi rather than -hu to harmonize with the preceding -i sound.)

18.meaning: 'A saying / word / statement' — an utterance or speech; that which is said.
18.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'a saying.' The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥ): it marks an indefinite noun in the accusative case, the form used for the object of a verb (e.g., 'to say a word') among other roles.

19.meaning: Kind / fitting / recognized as good — that which is commonly acknowledged as right and decent; honorable speech or conduct that accords with reason and custom. A rich term denoting what is universally seen as fair and proper.

parts.en: what is good / recognized as right

19.grammar: A passive participle (literally 'that which is known/recognized') used as a noun and adjective for goodness. The -an ending (accusative with nunation) commonly marks it as a direct object or a description ('in a fitting way'). The doubled-n sound signals indefiniteness ('a …').
19.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — knowing, recognizing; hence what is recognized and acknowledged as good

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
4.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: Pre-Islamic ignorance — the state and outlook of heedless, godless ignorance, especially the customs, pride, and false beliefs of the age before guidance. An abstract noun for that condition of unenlightenment.
7.grammar: A definite abstract noun formed with the -iyya suffix (which turns a word into a named state or "-ism"), here ending in -i, which is genitive. This ending typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… OF …") or follows a preposition.
7.root: ج-ه-ل (j-h-l) — ignorance, not knowing; also reckless, hot-headed behavior

8.meaning: The first, the foremost, the initial one — the feminine form of the ordinal 'first', denoting that which comes before all others in order or time.
8.grammar: A definite ordinal adjective (with al-, 'the'), the feminine of 'first', so it describes a feminine noun. It ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case; it conveys priority in sequence ('the first/former').
8.root: ا-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to precede, origin

10.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
10.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

12.meaning: The purifying alms (zakāt) — the obligatory portion given from one's wealth that purifies it and causes it to grow; an act of worship and social due.
12.grammar: A definite feminine noun (the tied tā' marks the feminine). The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the alms').
12.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure; to grow, increase, be blessed

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
14.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

15.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
15.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

16.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
16.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

17.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
17.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
17.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

21.meaning: A noun meaning 'filth', 'defilement', or 'abomination' — that which is impure, foul, or repugnant, whether physically unclean or spiritually corrupting.
21.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- (its 'l' assimilated into the following 'r', producing 'r-rijs'). The -a (accusative) ending typically marks it as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

22.meaning: People of / folk of — the people belonging to something, its members or family; those who hold or are associated with a thing (a place, a faith, a household).
22.grammar: A noun meaning 'people/folk of …,' normally joined to a following noun ('the people OF …'). The final -a (fatḥa) is the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or after certain particles.
22.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, people belonging to something

23.meaning: Al-bayt — the house, dwelling, or home; a place of residence or a building set apart, often used for a household or a place of worship.
23.grammar: A definite noun. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle. The word denotes a house, dwelling, or set-apart sacred building.
23.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — to spend the night; house, dwelling

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: It is recited / read aloud — a passage of revelation is being conveyed by being read out.
3.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ('it is being recited'). The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive (no doer named), and the final weak -ā shows it derives from a root ending in a weak letter; it conveys an ongoing action done to the subject.
3.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read aloud, follow

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: Signs, tokens, or evident proofs; also used for the discrete verses of revelation. An āya is a marker that points beyond itself to a deeper truth or to its Author.
7.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs/verses'). The sound-feminine plural takes -i in both the genitive and accusative; the -i ending here links it to a following noun ('… of …') or marks it as the object of a verb or preposition.

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: And the wisdom — sound judgment, deep understanding, and the placing of things rightly; knowledge joined to right action. It often denotes Allah-given insight or the wise content of revelation.
9.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the definite article 'the' attached to a feminine singular noun ('wisdom'). The -i ending is genitive, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

10.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
10.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

12.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The ones who submit/surrender — those who give themselves wholly to Allah in willing obedience and peace (the Muslims). As an active participle it names people characterized by this submission.
2.grammar: The prefix al- is 'the'. The stem is the Form IV active participle 'one who submits/surrenders'. The ending -īna is the sound masculine plural in the genitive/accusative state (the form used after prepositions, as object, or when linked to a preceding noun); its nominative counterpart would be -ūna. So: 'the ones who submit'.

5.meaning: And the believing women — the feminine plural of those who have faith, who place their trust and security in Allah and inwardly affirm the truth.
5.grammar: An active participle (one who believes) in the sound feminine plural. The prefix wa- means 'and'; al- is the definite article 'the'. The ending -āti is the sound feminine plural marker in its genitive or accusative form (the -i vowel rather than -u): it names a group of females and signals that the word is governed by a preceding preposition, oath, or verb, or is linked to a following noun.
5.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to have faith

6.meaning: And the devoutly obedient ones — those who stand in humble, sustained submission and devotion, constant in worship and obedience; 'the devout'.
6.grammar: A masculine active participle ('one who is devoutly obedient'), preceded by 'wa' ('and') and made definite by 'al-' ('the'), plural by '-īna'. The '-īna' form is the oblique plural, used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition. The root sense blends humble obedience with steady standing in devotion.
6.root: ق-ن-ت (q-n-t) — devout obedience, humble submission, constancy in worship

8.meaning: And the truthful ones — those who are honest and sincere, whose words and inner state match reality; 'the truthful'.
8.grammar: A masculine active participle ('one who is truthful'), preceded by the connector 'wa' ('and') and made definite by 'al-' ('the'), plural by '-īna'. The '-īna' form is the oblique plural, used when the noun serves as a direct object or follows a preposition.

10.meaning: 'And those who are patient / the steadfast' — people who endure hardship with calm, self-restrained perseverance, holding firm without complaint. Joined by 'and'.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and'), the definite article (its 'l' assimilated into the following sun letter 'ṣ'), the active participle 'one who is patient', and the sound masculine plural ending -īna. The active participle names the doer of the quality; the -īna ending marks the masculine plural in the genitive or accusative case.

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
22.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

23.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
23.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (nunation with fatḥa). The accusative typically marks a verb's object or an indefinite quantity, and the doubled-n sound shows the word is indefinite ('many').
23.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

25.meaning: He has prepared / made ready — to set something up in advance, to ready or get it in order beforehand.
25.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he prepared'). It belongs to the 'form IV' pattern (the a- prefix gives the sense of actively making something ready). With no added subject suffix, the bare form means 'he' did the action, completed in the past. The doubled middle letter (shadda) is part of this root.
25.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — to count, prepare, make ready

26.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
26.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

27.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
27.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

28.meaning: Forgiveness, pardon — the act of covering over and wiping away sins. Built on a sense of 'covering/shielding', it conveys both the concealing of faults and the remission of their consequences.
28.grammar: A verbal noun (the abstract notion of 'forgiving'). The ending -atan combines the feminine ending with the indefinite accusative marker (tanwīn). The accusative typically marks the noun as a direct object (the thing given or done), and the doubled-n sound ('nunation') signals that it is indefinite ('a/some forgiveness').

30.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
30.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: For / against a believer — one who has faith, who trusts and affirms; preceded by the preposition 'for/against.' The final -in (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a believer').
3.grammar: An active participle of Form IV (āmana, 'to believe'), meaning 'one who believes/has faith.' It is preceded by the preposition li- ('for/to'). The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation: genitive is the case taken after a preposition, and the nunation marks the noun as indefinite ('a believer').

4.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
4.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

6.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: "And His Messenger," the one sent with a message; "rasūl" denotes an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver something, here belonging to "Him."
9.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The base "rasūl" is a noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning "one who is sent." The suffix "-hu" is the attached possessive pronoun "his," placing the noun in a possessive "messenger of Him" relationship; the pronoun occupies the genitive slot.
9.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message or the one sent with it

10.meaning: A matter, affair, command, or thing to be done. It can mean an order issued or, more broadly, any business, situation, or decreed affair.
10.grammar: A noun in the accusative case with tanwīn (the -an ending), which marks it as indefinite and typically as the object of a verb ('a matter') or otherwise grammatically governed. The accusative shows it is being acted upon rather than acting.

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
11.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

12.meaning: '(That) He be / there be' — a form of the core verb 'to be/become', expressing existence or a state of being.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he is/becomes' or 'there is'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used after certain particles (e.g. 'that', 'so that', 'in order to') and giving the sense of a dependent or hoped-for action.
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to become

13.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
13.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

16.meaning: A compound: 'their affair' / 'their matter' / 'their command' — the word 'amr' (a matter, affair, command, or situation) joined to the pronoun 'their.'
16.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, which appears when the word follows a preposition or is possessed/linked to another word ('… of …'). The suffix '-him' is 'their' (masculine plural); its vowel is 'i' (not '-hum') precisely because it follows the genitive '-i.'

17.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
17.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

18.meaning: 'Disobeys' / 'rebels against' — to defy a command and refuse to comply, the opposite of obeying.

parts.en: vowel on the medial letter (weak final letter dropped)

18.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he disobeys'), in the jussive/conditional mood. The root ends in a weak letter (ي); in the jussive that final ي is dropped entirely as the mood marker, leaving the medial letter ص carrying its kasra (-i) at the word's end. The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject; the shadda on the yā' is an assimilation (idghām) carried over in recitation from a preceding word.

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

20.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
20.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

21.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
21.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

22.meaning: He strayed, lost the way, or went off course — to wander from the right path, whether literally or figuratively (to err, be misguided, or deviate from truth and guidance).
22.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he went astray'. The bare past-tense form with the -a ending signals a single male (or thing) as the doer of a completed action.
22.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

23.meaning: straying / error — the state of being lost from the right path, wandering far from guidance and truth. A verbal noun naming the condition of going astray.
23.grammar: A verbal noun (maṣdar) on the faʿāl pattern, naming the act/state of straying. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative — often used for the object of a verb or as an absolute object reinforcing a verb ('to stray a [great] straying') — and the -n shows it is indefinite.
23.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, get lost, err

24.meaning: An adjective meaning 'clear, plain, manifest' — describing something that is obvious and self-evident, or that makes things clear.
24.grammar: An active participle of form IV (mubīn), 'one that is manifest / makes clear.' The mu- prefix forms the participle. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative ending ('a clear one'), used here to agree with a preceding masculine accusative noun it describes.

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: You say / you were saying — a present-tense verb of speaking addressed to a single person. It expresses ongoing or habitual utterance.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person 'you' (masculine singular) subject, and the final '-u' is the indicative form, used for a plain ongoing statement ('you say'). The long 'ū' is the hollow root's middle letter surfacing.

3.meaning: 'to / for the One who…' — a preposition fused with a relative pronoun, introducing a clause that identifies someone by what they do ('the one who…').
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') joined to the masculine singular relative pronoun 'alladhī ('the one who/which'). A relative pronoun links to a following clause that describes its referent. Being a fixed particle, it does not change its ending for case.

4.meaning: 'He bestowed favor / blessed / granted bounty' — a completed act of conferring grace, blessing, and comforts upon someone.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb on the 'afʿala' pattern, with a built-in sense of conferring something upon another. Its form marks a single masculine 'he' as the doer, with no attached subject suffix. So: 'he bestowed favor'.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

6.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
6.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

8.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
8.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

10.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
10.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
13.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: 'Yourself / your own self / your soul' — the noun 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner being) carrying the possessive 'your' (single male).
16.grammar: The noun 'nafs' ('self/soul') with the second-person masculine-singular possessive ending '-ka' (here '-ika'): 'your self'. The attached possessive can sit on any case, so it alone does not mark subject or object.
16.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being of a person

17.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
17.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

21.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
21.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
21.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

22.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
22.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
22.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

23.meaning: An adjective meaning 'more entitled, having a better/greater right, more deserving' of something.
23.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the afʿal pattern, meaning 'more/most entitled'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word serves as the subject or as a predicate describing the subject.
23.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, just claim, what is due

24.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
24.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

26.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
26.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

27.meaning: He decreed, ordained, settled, or brought to a definitive conclusion — to decide a matter and carry it through so that it is fixed and accomplished. It carries the sense of an authoritative, final determination.
27.grammar: A past-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject — 'he' did the action, completed and in the past. There is no separate suffix; the bare verb form itself signals 'he'. The final root letter appears as a long 'ā' (written with a dagger alif) because this verb's third root letter is a weak vowel.
27.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decree, conclude, settle, and accomplish

29.meaning: From it / from her — marking the starting point or source out of which something comes, referring to a feminine or grammatically-feminine thing.
29.grammar: The preposition 'from/out of' attached to the pronoun -hā ('it/her'), which refers back to a feminine or grammatically-feminine noun. After a preposition this pronoun stands in the genitive (object) position, giving the sense 'from it' — the source or point of departure of an action.

32.meaning: A two-word particle phrase meaning "so that, in order that" — it introduces a purpose or intended result.
32.grammar: A compound purpose particle. It introduces a goal and causes the following present-tense verb to take the subjunctive mood (a verb ending in -a), expressing "in order that he may …". It does not change for person or number.

33.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
33.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

34.meaning: He/it is / he comes to be. A form of the verb kāna ('to be'), linking a subject to a state or asserting that something exists or occurs.
34.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 3rd person masculine; the final -a marks the subjunctive mood, the form a verb takes after particles meaning 'so that', 'in order to', or 'that'. It expresses a state being brought about rather than a plain fact.
34.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

35.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
35.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
35.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

36.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
36.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

37.meaning: Tightness, constriction, or distress of the heart — a sense of being hemmed in, hence unease, difficulty, or the kind of moral discomfort felt when something weighs on one. By extension it can mean blame or sin that constricts the conscience.
37.grammar: The -un ending (nunation) marks an indefinite noun ('a ___ / any ___') in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described as existing.

38.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
38.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

41.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
41.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

43.meaning: A small phrase meaning 'from them' or 'of them,' referring to a group of females. It combines the preposition min (from, of, some of) with an attached 'them' (feminine).
43.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. Min means 'from,' 'out of,' or 'some of.' The pronoun -hunna means 'them' for a group of females; after the n of min it keeps its base vowel -u (hunna). The combination commonly expresses source, origin, or a part taken from a whole.

45.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
45.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

46.meaning: 'Command, order, affair, matter.' This noun covers both a directive that is commanded and a situation or affair that comes to pass — what is decreed or what is the case.
46.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.

47.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
47.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

48.meaning: Passive participle of 'to do/make': 'done, carried out, accomplished.' It describes something that has been or will be brought into effect — an act fulfilled rather than left pending.
48.grammar: A passive participle on the pattern mafʿūl ('that which is done'). The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (the final 'tanwīn' n-sound), which commonly marks a predicate, an object, or a descriptive complement.
48.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — to do, to make, to act

1.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
1.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
3.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
3.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

4.meaning: The Prophet — a person who receives revelation from Allah and announces it, one given prophetic news and inspired tidings from the unseen.
4.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article 'the'. The final -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive chain, follows a preposition, or marks agreement with a preceding genitive word. The article's l assimilates into the following n (an-nabiy), since n is a 'sun letter'.
4.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; to inform, announce

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'constriction, hardship, blame, or discomfort' — a sense of being hemmed in, whether physical difficulty or moral fault.
6.grammar: A singular noun. The ending -in (genitive with nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a difficulty / any blame') and is the case typically used after a preposition.

7.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
7.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb whose core sense is 'to make obligatory, impose as a duty, ordain'; it also carries the related senses 'to appoint/allot a fixed share' and 'to undertake / bind oneself to a duty'. As shown, it means 'he made obligatory / he ordained'.
8.grammar: A completed (past) action in the basic faʿala pattern for a third-person masculine singular doer ('he/one [did it]'). There is no separable subject suffix on this form: the final fatḥa (-a) sitting on the last root letter is part of the verb stem itself, not an added ending, and the doer 'he' is understood from the pattern alone. A separate pronoun-suffix would appear only for other subjects (for example -tu 'I', -ta/-ti 'you', -tum 'you all').
8.root: ف-ر-ض (f-r-ḍ) — making obligatory; ordaining a fixed duty or share

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
9.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence.
