So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

11.meaning: An established way, practice, or norm; a consistent pattern of conduct that is followed as a precedent. When ascribed to Allah it denotes His unchanging way of dealing with creation.
11.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, marked by the final -a (often an object, or set as an emphatic statement). As the first term of a possessive pairing it links to a following noun, meaning 'the way of …'.
11.root: س-ن-ن (s-n-n) — to set a precedent; an established way

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
14.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

15.meaning: They were alone, withdrew in private, or were by themselves apart from others; to be in seclusion or privacy with someone.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb from a weak root, so the plural ending appears as -aw (written with a silent final alif). It means 'they' for a group of males and marks a completed action: 'they were alone / withdrew in private.'
15.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty, alone, secluded; privacy

16.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
16.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

17.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
17.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
17.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

18.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
18.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

19.meaning: 'Command, order, affair, matter.' This noun covers both a directive that is commanded and a situation or affair that comes to pass — what is decreed or what is the case.
19.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.

20.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
20.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: Messages — the communications or dispatches entrusted to be delivered; the plural of a single 'message'.
3.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt ending marks 'more than two' of a feminine word). The final -i is the ending that sound feminine plurals take in both the genitive ('of …' / after a preposition) and the object (accusative) roles — for this class of plural the two share one form.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: 'They fear' or 'they hold in awe' — experiencing khashya, a fear mixed with reverence and awareness of someone's greatness, especially the kind of dread that comes from knowledge of the one feared.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The -awna ending marks a masculine-plural 'they' subject (the long final root-vowel blends into the plural ending) and the indicative mood, which states the action as an ongoing or habitual fact.
7.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — fear blended with awe and reverence

8.meaning: Anyone / a single one: 'one' used to mean a sole individual, especially in negative or conditional contexts ('not anyone', 'any single person').
8.grammar: A noun meaning 'one / a single one', frequently used for 'anyone' when paired with a negation. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for a verb's object.

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

11.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
11.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
11.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

12.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
12.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
12.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

13.meaning: 'A reckoner / one who takes full account' — one who reckons, calculates, and holds to account, weighing every deed and giving each its exact due. It also carries the sense of being entirely sufficient as such an accountant.
13.grammar: A singular masculine noun/adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern (a thorough, capable reckoner). The ending -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, here marking the word as a specifying or circumstantial complement — telling in what capacity something is regarded ('as a reckoner'). The final nunation signals indefiniteness ('a…').
13.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to count, calculate, reckon, hold to account

1.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
1.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

3.meaning: Muḥammad — a masculine proper name meaning 'the praised one' or 'one worthy of much praise', built on the pattern of intensive/repeated praise.
3.grammar: A proper name of the passive-participle 'mufaʿʿal' (intensive) pattern, meaning 'highly praised'. The final -un (nunation) marks it as nominative — the case used for a subject or for the thing being identified/named.

5.meaning: One; anyone; a single individual. Often used in negative or conditional contexts to mean 'anyone (at all)'.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The -in ending combines the genitive marker -i (the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link, '… of …') with nunation (-n), the sign of an indefinite 'a / any'.

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

7.meaning: The plural noun 'men' joined to a 'your (plural)' pronoun — 'your men', i.e. the adult males of your community or group.
7.grammar: A plural noun (singular rajul, 'man') with the attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your', for a group). The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or when one noun is possessed by another ('… of …'); -kum makes it 'your men'.
7.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manhood, going on foot

8.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
8.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: 'The prophets' — those whom Allah selects to receive revelation and convey His message. The plural of nabī, a prophet who brings news from Allah.
12.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the genitive-or-accusative case — the form used when the noun is a direct object or governed by a preposition, as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject.
12.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; hence a prophet who brings news from Allah

13.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

15.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
15.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

16.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
16.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
16.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

17.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
17.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'Remember! / call to mind, mention' — a command to bring something to mind, keep it in memory, or speak of it.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you.' The '-ū' ending directs the order to a group ('you all remember!'); the initial connecting 'a-' is a helping vowel that lets the word begin.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: A mention, a remembrance, a reminder; calling something to mind or speaking of it, and by extension a piece of admonition or scripture.
6.grammar: A masculine verbal noun. The -an ending (tanwin) is the indefinite accusative, typically marking a direct object ('a remembrance') or a specification.
6.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to call to mind

7.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
7.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (nunation with fatḥa). The accusative typically marks a verb's object or an indefinite quantity, and the doubled-n sound shows the word is indefinite ('many').
7.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

2.meaning: Morning, daybreak, the early part of the day — the time from dawn until mid-morning.

parts.en: accusative ending on feminine noun (with nunation)

2.grammar: A feminine noun (its feminine ending is the tied-tā', pronounced '-t-' before the case vowel). The '-an' accusative ending here typically marks a time expression ('in the morning'), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.
2.root: ب-ك-ر (b-k-r) — early morning, to be early

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

4.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
4.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: Darknesses, layers of gloom; the manifold states of being deprived of light, whether literal or as a figure for ignorance and error.
8.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ("the darknesses"). The -i ending here is genitive — the case taken by this plural after a preposition (the -āt plural shows genitive with -i rather than the -a it would take in the accusative). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").
8.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; also wrongdoing and injustice

9.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
9.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

10.meaning: Light — radiance and illumination that dispels darkness; often a figure for guidance, truth, and clarity.
10.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ("… OF …"). The al- prefix makes it definite ("the").

11.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

12.meaning: With/in the believers — 'the believers' being those who have faith, who trust and affirm and are inwardly secure in belief. The word combines a preposition meaning 'with/by/in/toward' and the definite plural 'the believers'.
12.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with/by/toward') attached to the definite noun 'the believers'. The noun is in the genitive case — its sound masculine plural ending is -īna here — because words after a preposition take the genitive. The plural -īn(a) refers to three or more males (or a mixed group).

13.meaning: 'Most Merciful, ever-compassionate' — one who continually and abundantly shows mercy. On the faʿīl pattern it conveys a deep, settled, characteristic quality of mercy.
13.grammar: An adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern denoting a permanent trait. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a most merciful …'), commonly marking the object/complement of a verb or an adjective agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun.

1.meaning: Their greeting / salutation — the words of well-wishing and peace exchanged in welcome; here belonging to a group.
1.grammar: A noun (a Form II verbal noun meaning 'a greeting/wishing-of-life') ending in the nominative -u, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence. The attached -hum means 'their'. So: 'their greeting'.
1.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — to live; to greet with a wish of life

2.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
2.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
2.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

3.meaning: They meet / encounter it (or Him): a plural action of coming face to face with something or someone, often used of arriving at and confronting an appointed reckoning.
3.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, 3rd person masculine plural, from a weak-final (defective) root whose last letter is a yāʾ. In the singular this verb is yalqā; in the masculine plural the weak final letter drops and the plural ending -ūna fuses with the stem vowel to surface as the diphthong -awna (hence yalqawna, 'they meet'). The ya- prefix plus this plural ending mean 'they (masculine) do' an ongoing or yet-to-happen act. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it'.
3.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come upon

4.meaning: Peace, soundness, safety, well-being — freedom from harm and discord; a word of greeting and of the wholeness and security that comes from being safe and at peace.
4.grammar: A noun. The ending -un is the indefinite nominative: the -u marks the nominative (the form a subject or a stated/announced word takes), and the final -n ('tanwīn') marks it as indefinite ('peace', not 'the peace').

5.meaning: 'And He prepared / made ready' — a perfect verb meaning to ready, arrange, or set in store something in advance; here joined by 'and'.
5.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus a perfect verb (form IV), 3rd-person masculine singular. It states a completed act, 'he prepared'; the doubled final consonant reflects this form's pattern.

6.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

7.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
7.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
7.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

8.meaning: Noble, generous, honourable — describing something or someone of high worth, dignity, and openhanded goodness. Used of provision, status, or character that is precious and held in honour.
8.grammar: An adjective in the indefinite accusative. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks the indefinite accusative case, which typically signals the object of a verb or a descriptive/adverbial role, in an unspecified, non-particular sense ('a noble/generous one').

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: The Prophet — a person to whom Allah sends revelation and a divinely guided message for humankind. The word denotes one who conveys tidings from Allah, or (on another derivation) one of high and exalted rank.
2.grammar: A definite singular noun marked by the prefixed 'al-' ('the'). The doubling (shadda) on the nūn is not part of the base word: it results from the 'l' of 'al-' assimilating into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), so 'al-nabiyy' is pronounced 'an-nabiyy'. The base noun is نَبِيّ (nabiyy). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or the one being described.
2.root: Two derivations are held by grammarians: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, weighty information (one who brings tidings); or ن-ب-و (n-b-w) — to be high or elevated (one of exalted rank), favoured by those who note the doubled yāʾ pointing to an original wāw.

3.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
3.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

4.meaning: 'We sent you / We dispatched you' — the act of sending forth one male addressee, as one is sent on a mission or as a messenger.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV ('afʿala') pattern (to send), with two attached pronouns: 'nā' is the subject 'we,' and the final 'ka' is the object 'you' (one male). So it states a completed act, 'we sent you.'

7.meaning: One who warns; a herald who cautions of impending danger or consequence, urging heedfulness.
7.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and', joining this to what precedes. The stem is an intensive/agent noun on the faʿīl pattern, naming one who warns. The final -an (accusative with nunation) marks it indefinite and typically signals an object or a state/role ('as a …').
7.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution; a solemn vow/pledge

2.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
2.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: 'By His permission / with His leave'. It joins 'with/by' to the noun 'permission, leave, sanction' and an attached pronoun 'His', indicating something done by the authorization of the one referred to.
4.grammar: The prefix 'bi-' is a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by (means of)'. It places the following noun in the genitive case, shown by the '-i' ending. The attached '-hi' is a possessive pronoun, 'His' (or 'its'), so the whole reads 'by His permission'.
4.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, give leave; to hear/heed

1.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + a command 'give glad tidings, bring good news.' The verb means to announce something joyful that shows on the face — to cheer someone with happy news. It is the standard word for delivering good tidings.
1.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + an imperative (command) verb, addressed to a single male ('you, give good news'). The base form is bashshir; the final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word, not a case ending. The doubled middle letter marks an intensive/causative sense: actively bringing good news to someone.

2.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
2.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

3.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'because / by reason of the fact that'. It combines the preposition 'with/by' and anna ('that…'), together introducing a cause or explanation for what precedes.
3.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to the emphatic particle anna ('that…'). anna introduces and stresses a following statement and grammatically puts the noun after it into the accusative; the pairing as a whole signals 'because / due to the fact that'.

4.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
4.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

5.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
5.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: Bounty, grace, favour, or abundance; something good given freely and beyond what is owed. It can mean material provision (such as profit from trade) or divine grace and excess generosity.
7.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -an (accusative case with nunation) typically marks it as the direct object of a verb ('seeking a bounty') or as the goal of an action. The nunation also makes it indefinite ('a bounty / some favour').
7.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to be in excess, to surpass; hence grace, bounty, superiority

8.meaning: Large, great, big, or major — an adjective describing something of great size, amount, or importance. It can also mean elder/older in age. The -an ending leaves it indefinite ('a large …').
8.grammar: An indefinite adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn): it commonly marks the object of a verb, or works adverbially, and signals the word is indefinite ('a large one'). It pairs with ṣaghīr ('small').
8.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, largeness, being great or old

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

3.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
3.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

4.meaning: And the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief; people of a divided inner state who say one thing and hide another.
4.grammar: An active participle from Form III in the sound masculine plural. The prefix wa- means 'and'; al- is the definite article 'the'. The ending -īna is the sound masculine plural in its accusative or genitive form (the -ī vowel rather than -ū): it marks a group of males and signals that the word is a direct object, or is governed by a preposition or a preceding noun.
4.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — tunnel, hole; (Form III) to be two-faced, dissemble

7.meaning: And rely / and place your trust. A command (singular 'you') to entrust one's affairs fully to another and depend on Him completely, with calm reliance.
7.grammar: A masculine-singular command (imperative) addressed to one person: 'you, rely!'. It comes from a Form V verb pattern (tafaʿʿala) that conveys taking something fully upon oneself — here, deliberately committing one's reliance to another. The vowel-less ending (sukūn) is the normal final state of an imperative.
7.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — entrusting, reliance, appointing someone to manage one's affairs

8.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
8.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
8.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
10.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
10.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

11.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
11.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
11.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

12.meaning: A trustee, guardian, or disposer of affairs — one to whom matters are committed and who is relied upon to manage and protect them.
12.grammar: A noun on the intensive pattern faʿīl ('one who is relied upon'). The '-an' ending (with tanwīn) marks the indefinite accusative case: it commonly signals the object of a verb, or the role/capacity in which something serves ('as a …').
12.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — entrusting, reliance, appointing someone to manage one's affairs

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

6.meaning: Believing women — females who have faith, who trust and affirm Allah and His message and live in security of belief.

parts.en: feminine plural ending in the genitive/accusative (-āt → -i)

6.grammar: A feminine plural active participle ('women who believe') with 'the'. The sound feminine plural ending -āt takes -i rather than -u, marking the genitive or accusative — i.e. tied to a preceding preposition or noun, or serving as the object of an action, not as the active subject.
6.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security; faith, to believe and trust

7.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
7.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural, masculine) divorce / release them (women) from the marriage bond.' The form II pattern conveys carrying out the divorce decisively.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -tum marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all did'); it is lengthened to -tumū to connect to the following object pronoun -hunna, a feminine-plural object ('them'). The past tense states the action as completed or, in conditions, as supposed to have occurred.

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
10.grammar: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
10.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
11.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

12.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural, masculine) touch / make physical contact with' someone. In legal and intimate contexts the verb is frequently used as a delicate euphemism for sexual relations between spouses.
12.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix together with the -ū ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The attached -hunna is a feminine-plural object pronoun ('them' / 'those women'). The -ū without a following nūn reflects a subjunctive/jussive mood, the form taken after certain particles (e.g. negation or conditions).
12.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — touching, contact, feeling by hand

13.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
13.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

14.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
14.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

15.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them (a group of females).' It places a duty, burden, or claim 'on' a group of women — what is incumbent upon or held against them.
15.grammar: The preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') takes the form ʿalay- when an attached pronoun follows, often conveying obligation or something weighing upon someone. The suffix -hinna is the third-person feminine plural pronoun 'them,' for a group of females; the -i- vowel is the form the pronoun takes after this preposition.

16.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
16.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: The Prophet — a person to whom Allah sends revelation and a divinely guided message for humankind. The word denotes one who conveys tidings from Allah, or (on another derivation) one of high and exalted rank.
2.grammar: A definite singular noun marked by the prefixed 'al-' ('the'). The doubling (shadda) on the nūn is not part of the base word: it results from the 'l' of 'al-' assimilating into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), so 'al-nabiyy' is pronounced 'an-nabiyy'. The base noun is نَبِيّ (nabiyy). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or the one being described.
2.root: Two derivations are held by grammarians: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, weighty information (one who brings tidings); or ن-ب-و (n-b-w) — to be high or elevated (one of exalted rank), favoured by those who note the doubled yāʾ pointing to an original wāw.

3.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
3.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

5.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
5.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.

7.meaning: Those (women) who — a relative pronoun introducing a description, referring to a group of females and meaning 'the ones who…' or 'those females that…'.
7.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine plural: 'those (women) who.' It is indeclinable — its form does not change for case — and it links a following clause back to a feminine-plural group, much like English 'who/which/that' applied to women.

8.meaning: A second-person masculine singular past-tense verb meaning 'you gave' or 'you granted/bestowed.' It describes the act of handing over, conferring, or providing something to someone — often used of a gift or grant from one party to another.
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of Form IV (transitive, 'to give to'). The suffix -ta marks a second-person masculine singular subject, 'you (one man).' The whole form is rendered in plain past time: 'you gave / you have given.'
8.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in Form IV, to bring/give

9.meaning: A word meaning 'their wages / dues / rewards,' referring to a group of females. The base noun is the plural of 'wage, recompense, due reward,' joined to a 'their' (feminine) possessor.
9.grammar: A 'broken' plural noun (of ajr, 'wage/reward') carrying the accusative case-vowel -a, the ending used for the object of a verb. The suffix -hunna means 'their' for a group of females. The word denotes compensation or a rightful due owed in return for something.

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

11.meaning: It/she possessed, owned, or held in ownership — a completed act of having something under one's control or right.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb with the feminine ending -at: 'she/it possessed'. The -at marks completed action by a feminine singular subject. In the idiom 'what your right hands have possessed', the feminine subject is the (grammatically feminine) 'right hands'.
11.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, hold sway

13.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
13.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
15.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

16.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
16.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

25.meaning: Those (women) who — a relative pronoun introducing a description, referring to a group of females and meaning 'the ones who…' or 'those females that…'.
25.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine plural: 'those (women) who.' It is indeclinable — its form does not change for case — and it links a following clause back to a feminine-plural group, much like English 'who/which/that' applied to women.

30.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
30.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

33.meaning: To/for the Prophet — the one who receives and conveys revelation from Allah, a bearer of divine news to humankind. The leading 'to/for' particle links it to what depends on it.
33.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') + al- ('the') + 'prophet' (the l of al- assimilates into the following n, hence -nn-). The -i ending is genitive, the case regularly triggered by a preceding preposition like li- — 'to/for the prophet'.
33.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — to announce news; a prophet as bringer of tidings

34.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
34.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

35.meaning: A verb meaning 'he intended', 'he willed', or 'he meant' — to direct one's purpose toward something, to want or aim at it.
35.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the derived (form IV) pattern arāda. The bare stem with a final -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject, with the sense of actively willing or purposing something.
35.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, aim at

36.meaning: The Prophet — a person to whom Allah sends revelation and a divinely guided message for humankind. The word denotes one who conveys tidings from Allah, or (on another derivation) one of high and exalted rank.
36.grammar: A definite singular noun marked by the prefixed 'al-' ('the'). The doubling (shadda) on the nūn is not part of the base word: it results from the 'l' of 'al-' assimilating into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), so 'al-nabiyy' is pronounced 'an-nabiyy'. The base noun is نَبِيّ (nabiyy). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or the one being described.
36.root: Two derivations are held by grammarians: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, weighty information (one who brings tidings); or ن-ب-و (n-b-w) — to be high or elevated (one of exalted rank), favoured by those who note the doubled yāʾ pointing to an original wāw.

37.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
37.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

39.meaning: An adjective meaning 'pure / unmixed / exclusive' — something purely and solely one thing, free of any admixture, reserved for one party alone.
39.grammar: A feminine adjective (the ة marks the feminine form). The ending -an (written -tan with the feminine ة) is the indefinite accusative — the case often used for the object of a verb or for a descriptive/state word, and the extra -n (nunation) signals 'a/an', i.e. indefinite. It conveys '(being) purely/exclusively'.

40.meaning: 'To you / for you' — the preposition 'to/for' joined to the singular addressee 'you' (masculine). It marks direction, benefit, or possession ('belonging to you').
40.grammar: A preposition 'li-/la-' ('to, for') with an attached pronoun. The suffix -ka means 'you' (masculine singular). The fixed -a vowel on -ka is simply how this object pronoun is voweled; the whole unit means 'to/for you.' (The doubled 'l' reflects assimilation to a preceding word.)

41.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
41.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

42.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
42.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
42.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

43.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
43.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

44.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
44.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

45.meaning: We came to know, we have knowledge of, we recognize. The past-tense verb 'to know' with a first-person plural subject, expressing knowledge that has been attained or is established for 'us'.
45.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -nā here is the first-person plural subject ending ('we'), marking who performed the completed act of knowing.

46.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
46.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

48.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
48.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
48.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

49.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
49.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

51.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
51.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

52.meaning: It/she possessed, owned, or held in ownership — a completed act of having something under one's control or right.
52.grammar: A past-tense verb with the feminine ending -at: 'she/it possessed'. The -at marks completed action by a feminine singular subject. In the idiom 'what your right hands have possessed', the feminine subject is the (grammatically feminine) 'right hands'.
52.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, hold sway

53.meaning: Means "their right hands" — a plural of "right hand," which also carries connotations of oaths, pledges, and rightful possession.
53.grammar: A plural noun in the nominative case (the -u before the pronoun), the case used for a subject. The attached -hum means "their" (masculine plural). The word can denote either physical right hands or sworn oaths.
53.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand/side; oath; good fortune, blessing

55.meaning: He/it is / he comes to be. A form of the verb kāna ('to be'), linking a subject to a state or asserting that something exists or occurs.
55.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 3rd person masculine; the final -a marks the subjunctive mood, the form a verb takes after particles meaning 'so that', 'in order to', or 'that'. It expresses a state being brought about rather than a plain fact.
55.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

56.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
56.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

57.meaning: Tightness, constriction, or distress of the heart — a sense of being hemmed in, hence unease, difficulty, or the kind of moral discomfort felt when something weighs on one. By extension it can mean blame or sin that constricts the conscience.
57.grammar: The -un ending (nunation) marks an indefinite noun ('a ___ / any ___') in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described as existing.

58.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
58.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

59.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
59.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

60.meaning: A word meaning 'much-forgiving' or 'ever-forgiving' — an intensive form describing one whose forgiveness is abundant and constant. It is one of the qualities of Allah.
60.grammar: An intensive adjective on the pattern faʿūl, conveying that the quality is great in degree and repeated. The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite 'n' sound), written with a supporting alif; it is the form an indefinite word takes when it is, for example, a predicate of certain verbs/particles or otherwise placed in the object position.

61.meaning: 'Most Merciful / deeply compassionate' — an intensive form of raḥima, denoting one full of mercy and tender compassion; a frequent description of Allah.
61.grammar: An intensive adjective on the fa'īl pattern, expressing a deep, abiding quality — abounding in mercy. The -an ending is the accusative case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n,' often marking it as a predicate or as describing someone as 'most merciful.'

2.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
2.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

3.meaning: You will / You wish — to will, want, or choose that something be. Mashīʾa (the noun from this root) is sovereign volition; the verb names the act of willing or desiring a thing into being.
3.grammar: Present-tense verb addressed to a single masculine 'you'. The ta- prefix marks the second-person singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, the normal mood for a plain statement of fact ('you will / you wish').

4.meaning: A small phrase meaning 'from them' or 'of them,' referring to a group of females. It combines the preposition min (from, of, some of) with an attached 'them' (feminine).
4.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. Min means 'from,' 'out of,' or 'some of.' The pronoun -hunna means 'them' for a group of females; after the n of min it keeps its base vowel -u (hunna). The combination commonly expresses source, origin, or a part taken from a whole.

6.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
6.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

7.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
7.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

8.meaning: You will / You wish — to will, want, or choose that something be. Mashīʾa (the noun from this root) is sovereign volition; the verb names the act of willing or desiring a thing into being.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb addressed to a single masculine 'you'. The ta- prefix marks the second-person singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, the normal mood for a plain statement of fact ('you will / you wish').

9.meaning: And whoever / and the one who: 'and' joined to a word meaning 'who(ever)' — referring to a person or persons, often introducing a condition ('whoever does…') or a relative clause ('the one who…').
9.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the pronoun 'man' ('who / whoever'), which refers to people. 'man' itself does not change for case; the final -i is only a helping vowel added to avoid two unvowelled consonants meeting before the next word.

11.meaning: A compound meaning 'than one who / than whoever' — combining the preposition of comparison 'than' with the relative pronoun 'who', used to compare a person against others.
11.grammar: The preposition 'min' (here 'than', used after elatives) followed by the indeclinable relative 'man' ('who'). The final nūn of 'min' undergoes regressive assimilation into the following mīm of 'man', producing a doubled mīm; the resulting shadda sits on the mīm of 'man'. Both words are indeclinable particles and take no case ending.

13.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
13.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

14.meaning: Blame, sin, or fault — moral liability incurred by a wrong action; the sense of wrongdoing that counts against a person, or any leaning toward error.
14.grammar: A masculine noun. The final -a is the accusative case ending; this ending appears, among other uses, on the noun governed by a negating particle (as in the common construction 'there is no blame …').
14.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline, lean, tilt (toward wrong); hence fault/sin

15.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
15.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

16.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
16.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

17.meaning: Nearer, closer, or more fitting — a comparative meaning 'more likely to be the case' or 'more appropriate'. Also literally 'lower/nearest'.
17.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective ('nearer, more apt') on the af'al pattern. It ends in a fixed long -ā and does not change for case; it is also diptote (resisting the indefinite -n). It conveys that one option is closer to the goal or more suitable than another.

18.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
18.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

19.meaning: To become cool, settle, or be at rest; said of the eye, it means to be gladdened and consoled — for restlessness to cease and contentment to settle in (the idiom 'coolness of the eye' = joy and reassurance).

parts.en: to be cool / settle / be at rest

19.grammar: A present-tense verb with the prefix ta- marking a 'she/it' subject. The final -a reflects the subjunctive or jussive mood (the form taken after certain particles, e.g. 'so that' or a negation), rather than a plain statement. With 'the eye' as subject it forms the idiom for being gladdened and consoled.
19.root: ق-ر-ر (q-r-r) — to settle, be cool, come to rest, be content

21.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
21.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

24.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
24.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

27.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
27.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
27.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

28.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
28.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
28.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

29.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
29.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

30.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
30.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

31.meaning: Your hearts — the inner seat of feeling, intention, and understanding, belonging to a group of people.
31.grammar: A plural noun 'hearts' carrying the -i (genitive) ending because it is the first term of a possessive (iḍāfa) construction with the following pronoun -kum ('your', for a group). This noun-plus-pronoun pairing expresses possession: 'the hearts OF you all' = 'your hearts'. In Arabic the heart is understood as the center of both emotion and thought.
31.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, change

32.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
32.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

33.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
33.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

34.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
34.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

35.meaning: Forbearing and clement — one who is gentle and patient, who does not rush to punish despite having full power to do so; a quality of dignified restraint.
35.grammar: An intensive adjective (the faʿīl pattern) describing a deep, settled quality, in the indefinite accusative marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). The accusative often marks a predicate after certain verbs or particles. The word denotes calm, patient restraint that withholds anger or punishment.

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: A verb (imperfect) meaning 'it is lawful, it is permitted, it is allowed' — to be religiously/legally permissible.
2.grammar: Present/imperfect tense, third-person masculine singular ('it'). The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain statement of fact — an ongoing or general truth, not negated or made conditional.
2.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to be lawful, permitted, untied

3.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
3.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.
