7.meaning: Knowledge or awareness belonging to it — the act or content of knowing something, here possessed 'of it / about it'. Built on a noun meaning sure, established knowing, joined to a feminine 'it/her' possessor.
7.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun -hā ('its/her'). The -u on the stem is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified.

8.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
8.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
10.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hour' — most particularly the Last Hour, the appointed time of the world's end and the Resurrection; literally a portion of time, an hour, or a moment.
13.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- (its l assimilates into the following 'sun letter' s, hence the doubled s). The -a ending is the accusative case, the case typically taken by the direct object of a verb or by what follows certain particles.
13.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — a span of time, an hour; the appointed Hour

14.meaning: It is / it will be / so as to be — a verb of 'being', expressing existence or a state of being.
14.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person feminine singular ('it', e.g. a feminine thing). The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it' as the subject. The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement of being. From a hollow root whose middle و appears as the long ū.

15.meaning: An adjective meaning 'near, close, close at hand' — describing something short in distance, time, or relationship, easily reached or soon to come.
15.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern ('near, close'). The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (nunation), which typically marks the word as agreeing with an accusative noun it describes, or otherwise governed into the accusative; the tanwīn shows it is indefinite.

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
4.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

5.meaning: 'And He prepared / made ready' — a perfect verb meaning to ready, arrange, or set in store something in advance; here joined by 'and'.
5.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus a perfect verb (form IV), 3rd-person masculine singular. It states a completed act, 'he prepared'; the doubled final consonant reflects this form's pattern.

6.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

7.meaning: A blazing, fiercely kindled fire — flame that has been set ablaze and roars with intensity. The form conveys a fire that is made to burn violently.
7.grammar: A noun/intensive adjective. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, which typically signals a direct object or a descriptive complement governed into the accusative.
7.root: س-ع-ر (s-ʿ-r) — to kindle, to set ablaze, to make a fire flare up

1.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
1.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.

2.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
2.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

3.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
3.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: 'they find' — to come upon, obtain, or encounter something; to perceive a thing to be present or available.
5.grammar: A present/future verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ending -ūna combines the plural 'they' (-ū) with the indicative marker -na, signalling a simple ongoing or future statement (not negated or subjunctive). The ya- prefix marks the third person.
5.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, obtain

6.meaning: A guardian, protector, ally, or close supporter — one who is near and takes charge of another's affairs. Waliyy carries the sense of nearness combined with care, authority, and friendship.
6.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a protector'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case: it commonly marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as a predicate/complement after certain verbs of 'making' or 'becoming'.

7.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
7.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

8.meaning: 'A helper, supporter, one who gives aid and victory' — an intensive form stressing reliable, effective help.
8.grammar: An indefinite noun on an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that conveys a strong or constant doer — 'a true helper'. The -an ending marks the accusative and indefiniteness, commonly used here as a specifier naming the capacity ('as a helper').
8.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to give victory

1.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
1.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

3.meaning: Their faces — the plural 'faces' joined to a possessive 'their', i.e. the faces belonging to a group of people.
3.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u before the suffix is the nominative ending, marking the word as a subject or topic. The suffix -hum means 'their' (referring to a group of males or a mixed group): 'their faces'.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
5.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

6.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

7.meaning: "Oh, if only we …! Would that we …!" An exclamation of longing or regret: the call-particle "yā" intensifies the wish-word "layta" ("if only / would that"), with "us" as the ones wishing.
7.grammar: A wishing-particle expressing a longing for something contrary to fact or hard to attain ("if only …"). Layta belongs to the inna-family of particles, which place the following noun or pronoun in the accusative as their grammatical subject (the ism); so the attached -nā ("we/us") is layta's subject in meaning even though it takes the accusative form rather than the nominative an English subject would. The leading yā here is not a literal call but heightens the emotion of the wish.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
9.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

10.meaning: "and we obeyed / and we have complied" — wa- joins it on; the verb means to obey, submit to, and willingly comply with a command.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb with the subject suffix -nā meaning 'we.' Past tense presents the action as already completed ('we obeyed'); the -nā ending shows 'we' are the ones who did it.

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

2.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

3.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
3.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

1.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

1.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
1.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

3.meaning: Twofold, double, or two times over — twice the usual amount.
3.grammar: A dual noun (referring to exactly two). The '-ayni' ending marks the dual in the accusative/genitive — the special form Arabic uses for a pair, here meaning 'a double, twice as much'.
3.root: ض-ع-ف (ḍ-ʿ-f) — to double, multiply; a multiple, fold

4.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

5.meaning: The punishment, torment, or chastisement — severe penalty or suffering inflicted as retribution.
5.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the punishment') or follows a preposition.

8.meaning: Great, large, big — an adjective denoting magnitude, whether in size, importance, severity, or degree.
8.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The ending -an is accusative and indefinite ('a great …'); this 'tanwīn' often marks an indefinite adjective agreeing with an accusative noun, or an adverbial sense ('greatly').
8.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great, large, mighty

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: You (plural) are / you happen to be. A form of the 'hollow' verb kāna ('to be'), which links a subject to a state or description, or expresses simply being or existing.
5.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 2nd person; the -ū ending marks masculine plural. The dropping of the usual final -na (so takūnū rather than takūnūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form expected after conditional or subordinating particles.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

6.meaning: Like those who — a comparison particle joined to a relative pronoun, meaning 'similar to the ones who…' and pointing to a group defined by what follows.
6.grammar: A compound of the preposition ka- ('like, as'), expressing resemblance, and the masculine plural relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). The relative pronoun is fixed in form and introduces a description; it does not change for case.

8.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
8.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
10.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

11.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
11.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

12.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

13.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
13.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

14.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
14.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: 'Honored, eminent, held in high regard' — describing one who possesses prestige, standing, and a place of honor. Originally 'one whose face (wajh) is turned toward' — i.e., sought after and esteemed.
16.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn (nunation, the doubled 'n' sound marking indefiniteness — 'an honored one'). The accusative case is commonly used here for a circumstantial description (telling the state or condition in which someone is) or as a predicate of certain verbs.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: Be mindful and wary of — guard yourselves by placing a protective barrier between yourselves and harm or wrongdoing. This is the verb of taqwā: God-conscious caution that shields one from what is forbidden.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group ('you all'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you.' Built on a reflexive pattern (Form VIII), it conveys 'protect yourselves / be on guard.'

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: And say! / and speak! — a command to a group to utter or express something in words.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural command ('you all, say!'). Because it is a command, it has no subject prefix and drops the final -na that a plain statement ('you say') would carry; the silent alif after the -ū is just a spelling convention.

7.meaning: 'A saying / word / statement' — an utterance or speech; that which is said.
7.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'a saying.' The ending -an is the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥ): it marks an indefinite noun in the accusative case, the form used for the object of a verb (e.g., 'to say a word') among other roles.

8.meaning: Sound, upright, and well-aimed in speech — words that are straight, true, and hit the mark, neither crooked nor harmful. Used especially of speech that is correct, just, and to the point.
8.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern (which often gives an intensive or settled quality). The final -an is the indefinite accusative ('a sound/upright …'); the -n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite, and the accusative case typically signals it is the object of a verb or describes such an object.
8.root: س-د-د (s-d-d) — to be straight, on target, sound; to close a gap

2.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
2.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

4.meaning: A compound: 'and He will forgive' / 'and may He forgive'. It joins 'and' to an imperfect verb meaning to forgive, pardon, and cover over sins — to wipe away guilt and shield the wrongdoer from its consequences.
4.grammar: The wa- prefix is the connective 'and'. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The verb stands in the jussive mood — shown by its clipped, vowel-less ending — typically appearing after certain particles or as the result-clause of a condition ('… he will forgive / that he may forgive').
4.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, shield, and pardon; forgiveness

5.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

6.meaning: A compound: 'your (plural) sins'. The plural noun dhunūb ('sins, faults, misdeeds') with an attached possessive 'your (all)'. A 'sin' here is a fault or offense that incurs guilt.
6.grammar: Dhunūb is a broken (irregular) plural of dhanb, 'sin'. The -a ending marks the accusative case — typically the direct object of a verb ('… your sins' as the thing acted upon). The attached -kum is a possessive pronoun, second-person masculine plural, 'your (of you all)'.

7.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
7.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

8.meaning: 'Obeys' / 'complies with' — to follow and carry out the command of another, to be obedient.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he obeys'), in the jussive/conditional mood (a mood used after conditional or command particles). The base jussive ends in a silent consonant; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to avoid two unvowelled consonants meeting, not a case ending. The shadda on the yā' is an assimilation (idghām) carried over in recitation from a preceding word.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
9.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

10.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
10.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

11.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
11.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

12.meaning: He attained / triumphed — to win, succeed, and gain what one sought, especially salvation or deliverance; to come out victorious and safe.
12.grammar: A past-tense hollow verb (root f-w-z, pattern faʿala → fāza). It is third-person masculine singular, which takes a zero (no overt) subject suffix; the final '-a' is the inherent final vowel of the verb form, not a separable person marker. It denotes a completed act of winning or attaining success.

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'triumph, great success, winning, salvation' — a decisive attainment of what is sought together with deliverance from what is feared. It denotes the highest kind of winning, not merely a minor gain.
13.grammar: An indefinite masculine verbal noun. The '-an' ending (nunation with a final 'alif') marks it as indefinite ('a triumph') and as accusative — the case typically used for the object of a verb, or for a noun that specifies or reinforces an action (as in 'he triumphed a triumph,' i.e. 'a real triumph').

14.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
14.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
1.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

4.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
4.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
4.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

5.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

6.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
6.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

9.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
9.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

10.meaning: To bear it, to carry it — to take up and sustain a weight or burden; the verb ḥamala covers both physical carrying and the bearing of responsibility.

parts.en: bear / carry (imperfect verb stem, third person feminine plural)
it (third person feminine singular object pronoun)

10.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb from Form I of ḥ-m-l in the third-person feminine plural. The nūn al-niswah (-na) is the feminine plural subject suffix. The attached pronoun -hā is a third-person feminine singular object pronoun meaning 'it,' referring to al-amāna (the Trust, a feminine noun). The verbal phrase reads: 'they (f. pl.) bear/carry it.'
10.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, to bear, to transport; to bear a burden or responsibility

11.meaning: And they feared — to be apprehensive, to dread something; to feel reverential awe combined with caution. Ashfaqa implies a trembling concern or tender fear.

parts.en: they feared / were apprehensive (verb stem, Form IV, third person feminine plural past)

11.grammar: The conjunction wa- joins this clause to the preceding one. The verb ashfaqa is Form IV past tense of sh-f-q, with the third-person feminine plural suffix -na (nūn al-niswah). The Form IV pattern adds the meaning of entering into a state: 'to become filled with fearful concern.' Together: 'and they (f. pl.) feared/were apprehensive.'
11.root: ش-ف-ق (sh-f-q) — tenderness mixed with fear; apprehension; Form IV: to be apprehensive, to fear for something

12.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
12.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

13.meaning: And he/she/it bore it — to take up and carry a burden, whether physical weight or moral/spiritual responsibility.

parts.en: he/she bore / carried (Form I past tense verb)
it (third person feminine singular object pronoun)

13.grammar: The conjunction wa- here introduces a contrast ('but'). The verb ḥamala is third-person masculine singular past tense, Form I of ḥ-m-l. The attached pronoun -hā is a feminine singular object pronoun referring to al-amāna (the Trust). The form reads: 'and he bore it' — contrasting with the preceding refusal of others.
13.root: ح-م-ل (ḥ-m-l) — to carry, to bear, to transport; to bear a burden or responsibility

14.meaning: 'Mankind, the human being, humanity' — the human as a species or as the representative human creature.
14.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') here generalises to the whole class ('humankind as such'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the subject (the doer or the thing spoken about) of a sentence.
14.root: ا-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar; humankind

15.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
15.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

16.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

16.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

17.meaning: Deeply unjust, gravely wrongdoing — one who habitually or intensely wrongs others or their own soul; a hyperbolic form indicating extreme injustice.

parts.en: one who is deeply/excessively unjust (intensive adjective stem)

17.grammar: The form ẓalūm follows the pattern faʿūl, which in Arabic is an intensive adjective (ṣīghat al-mubālagha) indicating excess or habitualness of the quality — here, extreme injustice or persistent wrongdoing. The -an ending is tanwīn fatḥ, marking it as indefinite and in the accusative case, functioning here as a predicate or circumstantial description.
17.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, to be unjust, to oppress, to put a thing in the wrong place

18.meaning: Deeply ignorant, profoundly heedless — one who is habitually or intensely unaware; the pattern suggests not mere lack of knowledge but willful or ingrained heedlessness.

parts.en: one who is deeply/excessively ignorant (intensive adjective stem)

18.grammar: The form jahūl follows the pattern faʿūl, an intensive adjective (ṣīghat al-mubālagha) signifying extreme or habitual ignorance and heedlessness. The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) marks indefiniteness and the accusative case. It pairs with ẓalūman as a doubled predicate or description, characterizing the subject in the most emphatic possible terms.
18.root: ج-ه-ل (j-h-l) — to be ignorant, to be heedless, to lack knowledge or awareness

1.meaning: So that He may punish — in order that punishment be administered; the verb ʿadhdaba means to inflict severe pain or torment as a consequence of wrongdoing.

parts.en: so that / in order to (purpose preposition/particle)
He may punish / torment (Form II imperfect verb, third person masculine singular)

1.grammar: The particle li- before an imperfect verb introduces a purpose clause, meaning 'in order that' or 'so that.' The verb yuʿadhdhiba is Form II (faʿʿala pattern) third-person masculine singular imperfect in the subjunctive mood (manṣūb), signaled by the -a ending instead of the default -u. The subjunctive after li- is grammatically required in Arabic to express purpose. Form II intensifies the action: severe, deliberate punishment.
1.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, to inflict pain or torment; Form II: to punish severely

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief; people who present one face publicly and hide another within. From a root evoking a tunnel with two openings, suggesting a hidden way out.
3.grammar: A definite noun: al- means 'the'. 'Munāfiq' is an active participle of Form III ('one who behaves hypocritically'). The ending -īna marks the masculine sound plural in the oblique case (the form used for objects of verbs and after prepositions, i.e. accusative/genitive, as opposed to nominative -ūna).
3.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — tunnel/burrow with a hidden exit; hence hypocrisy

4.meaning: 'And the hypocrites (women)' — the feminine plural counterpart of the male hypocrites: women who outwardly profess faith while concealing disbelief. The leading 'and' joins them to what precedes; this is the definite feminine plural in the object/oblique form.
4.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun, with wa- ('and') and al- ('the') prefixed. The -āt is the feminine plural marker, and the final -i is the accusative/genitive case — the form used for a direct object, after a preposition, or linked to a preceding noun. (In a sound feminine plural this same -i serves both the object and the genitive, contrasting with -u for the subject.)
4.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — a tunnel with two exits; hence hypocrisy (a hidden second way out)

5.meaning: And the male polytheists — those men who associate partners with Allah; mushrik denotes one who commits shirk, the gravest sin in Islam, that of attributing partners or equals to Allah.

parts.en: male polytheists / those who associate partners (with Allah) (masculine plural noun)

5.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural noun. The sound masculine plural in Arabic takes the ending -ūna in the nominative and -īna in both the accusative and genitive. The form mushrikīna (ending in -īna) therefore indicates either accusative or genitive case — agreeing with surrounding nouns in its grammatical position. The stem mushrik is the active participle of Form IV of sh-r-k, meaning 'one who associates (partners with Allah).'
5.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — partnership, sharing; Form IV (ʾashrak): to associate partners with Allah; shirk: polytheism

6.meaning: And the female polytheists — those women who associate partners with Allah; the feminine counterpart to al-mushrikīna.

parts.en: female polytheists (feminine sound plural noun stem)

6.grammar: A definite feminine sound plural noun. The feminine sound plural is formed with the suffix -āt, and it takes a kasra (-i) in both the genitive and accusative cases (unlike masculine sound plurals, the feminine sound plural uses -in / -ātin for indefinite and -i / -āti for definite in non-nominative positions). The -i ending here marks genitive (or accusative), agreeing in case with surrounding nouns in the context.
6.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — partnership, sharing; Form IV (ʾashrak): to associate partners with Allah; shirk: polytheism

7.meaning: 'And that He may turn in mercy / accept repentance' — and that He may relent toward and accept the return of one who repents. Said of Allah, it means He grants pardon and welcomes the penitent back.
7.grammar: Connector wa ('and') + a present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he'. The -a ending (-tūba) is the subjunctive, carried over from a preceding 'so that' purpose, giving 'and that He may turn (in mercy)'. The root means 'to turn/return': of a servant it is repenting; of Allah it is relenting and accepting that repentance.
7.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, return; repentance, and Allah's acceptance of it

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
9.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
9.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

10.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
10.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

11.meaning: And the believing women — the feminine plural of those who have faith, who place their trust and security in Allah and inwardly affirm the truth.
11.grammar: An active participle (one who believes) in the sound feminine plural. The prefix wa- means 'and'; al- is the definite article 'the'. The ending -āti is the sound feminine plural marker in its genitive or accusative form (the -i vowel rather than -u): it names a group of females and signals that the word is governed by a preceding preposition, oath, or verb, or is linked to a following noun.
11.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to have faith

12.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
13.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

14.meaning: A word meaning 'much-forgiving' or 'ever-forgiving' — an intensive form describing one whose forgiveness is abundant and constant. It is one of the qualities of Allah.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective on the pattern faʿūl, conveying that the quality is great in degree and repeated. The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite 'n' sound), written with a supporting alif; it is the form an indefinite word takes when it is, for example, a predicate of certain verbs/particles or otherwise placed in the object position.

15.meaning: 'Most Merciful' / 'Ever-Merciful' — an intensive adjective describing one whose mercy is constant, deep, and abundantly poured out. As a divine attribute it points to Allah's enduring compassion toward His creation.
15.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which signals an abundant, lasting quality ('ever-/most merciful'). The tanwīn fatḥ (-an) marks it as indefinite and accusative; here it stands as an accusative predicate complement (the quality affirmed of the one described). The shadda on the rāʾ (رَّ) reflects assimilation of a preceding definite article's lām (l + r → rr) at the word junction in recitation.
